plan: Store the input dictionary via copy.deepcopy in __init__ so the workspace owns an isolated tree; to_data() returns another deepcopy so callers can never alias internal state.

Write one recursive generator (_walk) that yields (item, depth) in document order for containers (section/group); build total_word_count, unresolved_markers, and outline as thin folds over that single traversal.

Parse note text with two compiled regexes: markers are exactly [[?identifier]] with a \w+ identifier; word counting first substitutes markers out of the text, then counts \b\w+\b runs, so marker syntax and identifiers never count as words. References contribute their declared word_count and their unresolved list.
unresolved_markers merges note-marker identifiers and reference unresolved entries into a set, then returns sorted(set) for unique lexicographic order.
outline emits the workspace title, then '  ' * level + '<kind>: <title>' with top-level items at nesting level 1, using the same deterministic traversal.

Implement move as validate-then-mutate: resolve the item (parent list + index) and the destination list, check string-typed ids, existence, container-ness, self/descendant containment, and index bounds all before touching the tree; only after every check passes, pop from the source list and append/insert into the destination. Any raised ValueError therefore leaves to_data() bit-for-bit unchanged.
Detect illegal containment by scanning the moved item's own subtree for the destination id (covers moving a container into itself or any descendant).
mechanisms: Deep-copy isolation at both the constructor and to_data boundary
Single recursive document-order generator shared by all read operations
Marker-stripping regex pipeline (substitute [[?id]] tokens, then count \b\w+\b)
Set-union plus sorted() for unique lexicographic marker identifiers
Depth-scaled two-space indentation driven by traversal depth
Validate-then-mutate move protocol guaranteeing atomicity on failure
Subtree scan for self/descendant containment rejection
